prompt: Why is the list of requirements written before anybody reads a provider's sales page?
hint: Against what are the answers compared?

choices.text: So they meet Tarefa's needs, not each other
choices.why: Right: the answers are compared with Tarefa's needs, and a MUST written first is not renegotiated in the meeting.

choices.text: Sales pages are not allowed as sources
choices.why: They may be read; the order is the point.

choices.text: Providers refuse to answer after reading one
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: The list must match the provider's own format
choices.why: The list is Tarefa's, in Tarefa's terms.

prompt: What separates a MUST from a SHOULD in `requirements.json`?

choices.text: A MUST carries a number and a SHOULD does not
choices.why: `dpa` is a MUST with no number.

choices.text: SHOULDs are added up and MUSTs are not counted
choices.why: Half of it; the other half is what a failed MUST does.

choices.text: A failed MUST rules a provider out
choices.why: Right: a SHOULD only counts in its favour, and the two are never added together.

choices.text: MUSTs come from the law and SHOULDs from Tarefa
choices.why: Both are Tarefa's decisions, some because of the law.

prompt: Why must a provider report an incident within 48 hours?
hint: Tarefa has a deadline of its own.

choices.text: The provider's audit report requires it
choices.why: The audit is about the provider's controls, not Tarefa's deadlines.

choices.text: Tarefa has three working days to tell the ANPD
choices.why: Right: a later notice leaves Tarefa no time.

choices.text: Clients are told of every incident within 48 hours
choices.why: The requirement is about the regulator's deadline.

choices.text: Prompts are deleted after 48 hours anyway
choices.why: Retention is 30 days at most, another requirement.

prompt: Match each requirement to the reason the lesson gives for it.
hint: One reason on the right belongs to no requirement.

pairs.right: text could resurface in replies to other customers
processing abroad is an international transfer
a changed model changes everything measured

right_distractors: a shorter contract is easier to read

prompt: Under the LGPD, a provider acting on Tarefa's instructions is an ___.
How many of the three providers does `guard vendor` mark `in`?
`provider-a` meets every SHOULD. Why is it out?

choices.text: Its audit report is out of date
choices.why: Its SOC 2 report is from 2026.

choices.text: It processes data in the United States
choices.why: `US` is one of the allowed regions.

choices.text: It has no data processing agreement
choices.why: It signed one on 2026-03-10.

choices.text: Its incident notice takes 72 hours
choices.why: Right: past Tarefa's own deadline, and a MUST.

prompt: `provider-b` trains on customer data unless the customer opts out. What does the lesson say can happen next?
hint: A MUST can be a question.

choices.text: Tarefa accepts it, since opting out is probably enough
choices.why: That is the one thing the lesson rules out.

choices.text: Tarefa drops it for good, as the MUST failed
choices.why: A failing MUST can sometimes be fixed by contract.

choices.text: A signed clause turns training off
choices.why: Right: then the list is run again, the answer changes, and its evidence becomes the clause.

choices.text: The MUST becomes a SHOULD for this provider
choices.why: Moving the line for one provider is renegotiating it.

prompt: Why does `vendor.py` keep MUSTs and SHOULDs apart instead of adding them into one score?

choices.text: A single score would rank `provider-a` first
choices.why: Right: and it fails a MUST.

choices.text: MUSTs cannot be expressed as numbers
choices.why: They could be; the reason is what a sum would hide.

choices.text: SHOULDs are too few to matter
choices.why: They matter among providers that pass.

choices.text: The program has no room to print a sum
choices.why: Space is not the reason.

prompt: What does `vendor.py` decide about price, quality and latency?

choices.text: Price only, once the MUSTs pass
choices.why: It never reads a price.

choices.text: Latency, from the region of each provider
choices.why: The region is a legal question here, not a speed one.

choices.text: All three, through the SHOULD score
choices.why: The SHOULDs are about data and contracts.

choices.text: Nothing; they are compared later
choices.why: Right: it only keeps failing providers out of that comparison.

prompt: How many of `provider-c`'s passing answers have no evidence?
`provider-c` passes `training` and `retention_days` on its word. What does the lesson require before signing?
hint: Where do the answers have to be written?

choices.text: A second questionnaire with the same questions
choices.why: A second answer is a second claim.

choices.text: Both, written into the contract
choices.why: Right: the evidence column then names a clause.

choices.text: An audit report from another provider
choices.why: Another provider's report says nothing about this one.

choices.text: A screenshot of the provider's website
choices.why: A website can change tomorrow.

prompt: Which kinds of evidence does the lesson rank above a page on the provider's website? Choose all that apply.
hint: What binds, and who else says it.

choices.text: a contract clause
choices.why: Yes: it binds the provider.

choices.text: an independent audit report
choices.why: Yes: somebody other than the provider says it.

choices.text: a signed data processing agreement
choices.why: Yes: it is part of the contract.

choices.text: a sales conversation
choices.why: The lesson says it is not evidence at all.

choices.text: the provider's answer to the questionnaire
choices.why: That is the claim being checked.

prompt: A provider's SOC 2 Type II report covers its billing platform. What does the lesson say to check before relying on it?

choices.text: Nothing, since SOC 2 Type II is the strongest report
choices.why: Strength means nothing outside the report's scope.

choices.text: Only the date it was issued
choices.why: The period matters, and so does the scope.

choices.text: The period and the scope it covers
choices.why: Right: a billing system says nothing about where prompts are kept.

choices.text: That it was paid for by the provider
choices.why: Providers always pay for their audits; that is not the test.

prompt: When does the lesson say the assessment is run again?

choices.text: Only when the contract is up for renewal
choices.why: Terms can change in the middle of a contract.

choices.text: Whenever a new model is released by anybody
choices.why: Other companies' releases are not the trigger.

choices.text: Every week, automatically
choices.why: The lesson asks for less, but with a second trigger.

choices.text: Every year, and whenever its terms change
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Put the steps of choosing a provider in the order the lesson takes them.
items: Write the MUSTs and SHOULDs before reading any offer
Collect each provider's answers with their evidence
Rule out every provider failing a MUST
Put the unbacked answers that matter into the contract
Compare price and quality among those left

prompt: Why does the lesson call being unable to leave a provider a security question?
hint: What happens the day it stops meeting a MUST?

choices.text: Switching providers is itself a security incident
choices.why: Leaving is a planned change, not an incident.

choices.text: Leaving must be possible that day
choices.why: Right: otherwise the failed MUST is simply accepted.

choices.text: Every provider deletes data when a contract ends
choices.why: That is a SHOULD here, and needs evidence.

choices.text: A pinned model cannot receive security fixes
choices.why: Pinning is about notice before retirement.
